notes.summary: An independently admissible polar-measure sector reconstructs richer positive currents on Bl_p(P1×P1), with order, scaling, constants, modification compatibility and decreasing approximation. This restricted analytic sector does not solve full P14.4.
notes.detailedSummary: Geometric states (a,b,c,ν,κ) use atomless positive measures satisfying an explicit logarithmic-kernel admissibility condition, rather than original complex potentials. They reconstruct θ-psh weights in actual big non-nef classes and retain the diffuse polar current discarded by nonpluripolar products. A local factorization/Jensen proof establishes exponential integrability after every given smooth modification. The construction has compatible current pullbacks and an actual decreasing approximation, but depends on a prescribed fibration, lacks maximum closure, and establishes no arbitrary transcendental extension or DXZ/MP operator comparison.
notes.text:
This is proved partial geometric progress, not a solution of unchanged original P14.4. The deliverables are P14.4-paper.tex, P14.4-paper.pdf, P14.4-argument.md, supporting-notes.json and source-application-ledger.json. These remain unverified mathematical drafts.

Use dd^c=(i/2π)∂∂bar. On P1 with unit Fubini–Study form ω, let G(z,t)=log(|z−t|²/((1+|z|²)(1+|t|²)))≤0, with dd^c_zG=δt−ω. An admissible input is a finite positive atomless measure ν supported on a compact affine set S, satisfying ∫G(x,t)dν(t)=−∞ for every x∈S. Zero is allowed. Positive sums and scalings preserve admissibility by the kernel sign and support unions. This condition does not require an original complex potential.

Set m=ν(P1), Uν=∫Gdν. Uniform local logarithmic L1 bounds and Fubini prove local integrability and dd^cUν=ν−mω. Fatou gives upper semicontinuity, integrated submean inequalities give the canonical quasi-psh representative, and differentiation off S proves smoothness there. Its poles are precisely S; hence S is polar and area-null.

For every h>0, e^(−hUν) is locally integrable. Restrict ν near a support point to mass δ<1/h, using atomlessness. Jensen bounds the exponential of its logarithmic potential by δ^−1∫|z−t|^(−2hδ)dν(t). Fubini and hδ<1 give integrability; the complementary contribution is bounded on a smaller disc.

This conclusion survives every nonconstant holomorphic pullback f. At a point with f-value t0∈S, choose a complex line on which f(z,0)−t0 has finite order d. A small-circle argument-principle homotopy factors f(z,w)−t=u∏_{i=1}^d(z−r_i), with roots inside the half-disc and a uniformly bounded-below zero-free unit. The unit bound follows on the outer circle and then from the maximum principle for 1/u. Hölder bounds ∫|f−t|^(−2ε) uniformly when dε<1. Choose restricted ν-mass δ<1/(hd), apply Jensen and Fubini. The same factorization supplies local logarithmic L1 bounds. Thus pulled local psh primitives are legitimate and exponentially integrable to every order; no projective resolution or pullback of arbitrary distributions is assumed.

Let π:X=Bl_(∞,∞)(P1_z×P1_w)→Y, E exceptional, q=pr_z∘π and r=pr_w∘π. Choose e=log|σE|²_h≤0 and ρ=c1(O(E),h), so dd^ce=[E]−ρ. Define states D=(a,b,c,ν,κ), a,b,c≥0, m≤b, κ real. The enriched carrier is V_X×P1(C), projecting to the specified centered ideal-semivaluation point set V_X. Retain ν as its positive functional on continuous tests on the slice over v0; continuous cutoffs and regularity reconstruct the measure. No MP topology identification is presumed.

For a,b,c>0, reconstruct α=bH_z+cH_w+aE, θ=bq*ω_z+cr*ω_w+aρ, ΦD=ae+Uν∘q+κ, and TD=a[E]+(b−m)q*ω_z+cr*ω_w+q*ν. Define q*ν through its pulled local psh primitives, proving positivity. The class is big: A=2(H_z+H_w)−E is the hyperplane class of the graph/Segre embedding of the blowup into P3×P2. The hyperplanes through the blown-up point generate its ideal. For t=min(b,c), α=(t/2)A+(b−t)H_z+(c−t)H_w+(a+t/2)E gives a Kähler current. Since E²=−1 and pullbacks have degree zero on E, α·E=−a<0, proving non-nefness.

On each fixed (a,b,c) leaf, exact order is Uν+κ≤Uν′+κ′ at every base point. It equals ΦD≤ΦD′ because q has points outside E above every base point. Addition and positive scaling give actual sums and scalings of currents and primitives; zero coefficients are defined separately. Constants act through κ. Rooftop competitor scaling proves P_(λθ)[λu]=λPθ[u] for λ>0; shifting the envelope parameter proves invariance under input constants. Fiber integration of TD−a[E] against ω_w gives (b−m)ω_z+ν, whose area-singular part reconstructs ν.

For every given smooth proper bimeromorphic p:W→X, ΦD∘p gives TD,W=a[p*E]+(b−m)(q∘p)*ω_z+c(r∘p)*ω_w+(q∘p)*ν. Actual pulled sections and primitives compose, retaining every multiplicity. The carrier map is (v,z)↦(p_*v,z), with (p_*v)(I)=v(I O_W); it composes, retains support by contraction and preserves the measure on the generic slice. Under θ′=θ+dd^cf, transport Φ to Φ−f and an obstacle h to h−f. Competitors give Pθ′(Φ−f+C,h−f)=Pθ(Φ+C,h)−f. Resetting the obstacle to zero is a different reference choice.

For every real t>0, I(tΦD)=O_X(−floor(ta)E). Near E the polar term is smooth; radial integration gives j+1>ta for a germ vanishing to order j. Expansion of an arbitrary germ proves necessity. Off E use exponential integrability. Consequently QD(v)=−lim_l l^−1v(I(lΦD))=−a v(I_E) on all semivaluations, including supports: finite values follow from floors, infinite values from eventually positive ideal powers; the unit ideal has value zero. QD(v0)=0. On every W, I(tΦD∘p)=I(ta e∘p). For SNC p*E this is its componentwise floor divisor ideal; no incorrect floor formula is asserted for a non-SNC divisor.

For k=1,2, <TD,W^k>=(p*SD)^k, where SD=(b−m)q*ω_z+cr*ω_w. Essential external input is BEGZ, literal arXiv:0812.3674v2, §1.2: nonpluripolar locality/noncharging and the local criterion that finite complement-product mass gives the trivial extension for potentials locally bounded off a closed complete pluripolar set. Here that set is p^−1E∪(q∘p)^−1S. The complement current is smooth. Smooth coefficient measures do not charge the pole set: use submersion coordinates and Fubini off the analytic critical locus, and area-null analytic sets on that locus. The complement product has finite local mass, checking applicability without assuming W Kähler. Thus raw mass is exactly 2c(b−m), unchanged on W by change of variables on its isomorphism locus.

Asymptotic shadows add; exact ideal floors need not. Constants, ν, ordinary P-data and raw mass are forgotten by Q. At fixed class ν_j=(1−1/j)ν, j≥2, gives actual admissible states with ΦD_j decreasing everywhere to ΦD. Total variation error is m/j; products and masses converge by their explicit polynomial formulas. Uniform logarithmic bounds give continuity from total variation to local L1 on each fixed modification for common compact affine support.

Limitations: this is a separated-current analytic geometric sector with a fixed fibration and forms. It lacks maximum closure, arbitrary P-type realization, compatible DXZ test curves, PL/model approximation and MP operator comparison. Its real parameters lie in real Néron–Severi space, not genuinely transcendental classes. Rerun python check_evidence.py and latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error P14.4-paper.tex; these checks do not certify the analytic proofs.

notes.summary: The mandatory example is independently reconstructed and strengthened: all multiplier ideals and first/top nonpluripolar products agree on every smooth modification, while normalized ordinary P-envelopes differ.
notes.detailedSummary: Explicit atomless Cantor measures on disjoint supports give ν_i=sμ_i with identical entire ideal and nonpluripolar-product towers and positive raw mass 2c(b−s). Their bounded maximum has mass 2bc. DDL monotonicity and positive-mass envelope membership therefore exclude equal normalized P-envelopes. At a=s=1/2, b=c=1 this gives H+(1/2)E and mass one. The retained geometric measures distinguish the states. This defeats the specified tower, not every possible movable datum or original P14.4 itself.
notes.text:
This result uses the reconstruction, pullback integrability and product computation proved in n1. The earlier partial paper is not assumed as a theorem. The proof is in P14.4-paper.tex, Section 6, and P14.4-argument.md, Section 8.

Starting from [0,1], retain two endpoint intervals with successive lengths ℓ_j=exp(−4^j). Children are disjoint because 2e^−4<1 and log 2<3·4^j thereafter. Their intersection is C. Bernoulli measure μ0 assigns each level-j interval mass 2^−j; every singleton has mass at most 2^−j for all j, hence zero. Translate μ0 to C+2 to obtain μ1. Both supports are compact, disjoint and avoid infinity. For x in its level-j interval, the nonpositive spherical kernel gives Uμ0(x)≤2^−j·2 log ℓ_j=−2·2^j→−∞. The translated estimate is identical. Thus both measures satisfy n1's independent admissibility condition.

Fix a,b,c>0 and 0<s<b in α=bH_z+cH_w+aE. Set Φ_i=ae+sUμi∘q. By n1, all real-scale ideals on X are O_X(−floor(ta)E), and on every given smooth modification p:W→X they are I(ta e∘p), independently of i. Their first and second nonpluripolar currents on W are both (p*S_s)^k, k=1,2, with S_s=(b−s)q*ω_z+cr*ω_w. The common positive raw mass is 2c(b−s). These equalities cover the entire smooth-modification tower.

The curve maximum max(Uμ0,Uμ1) is bounded: near either support the other function is smooth and bounded below; elsewhere use compactness. Therefore W=max(Φ0,Φ1) differs boundedly from ae and is θ-psh by the local psh maximum rule.

The exact external mass input is DDL, arXiv:1705.05796v3, Theorem 2.4: on a compact Kähler n-fold, for smooth closed real θ_j and canonical u_j,v_j∈PSH(X,θ_j), inequalities v_j≤u_j+C_j imply that the total mixed nonpluripolar mass of the u_j is at least that of the v_j. Applying both directions to W and ae gives Mθ(W)=2bc. Its §3.2 membership assertion gives φ≤Pθ[φ]≤0 and Mθ(Pθ[φ])=Mθ(φ) for the nonpositive positive-mass inputs used here. Complete pertinent proof units, including Theorem 2.3, were read in literal v3 and frozen in sources/DDL-pertinent-units.txt; the ledger records URLs and payload hashes.

All hypotheses are checked: n1 proves X compact Kähler and α big; Φ_i and W are canonical θ-psh; the inputs are nonpositive; 0<s<b gives positive mass. Translate DDL's Hessian convention by dividing its potentials, obstacles and constants by 2π. No zero-mass envelope theorem, small-unbounded-locus restriction or envelope/max identity is used.

If the normalized envelopes were a common P, membership gives Φ_i≤P and Mθ(P)=2c(b−s). Then W≤P and monotonicity forces 2bc≤2c(b−s)<2bc, impossible. The retained measures sμ_i distinguish these states.

For a=s=1/2 and b=c=1, α=H+(1/2)E; ideals are O_X(−floor(t/2)E), first product (1/2)q*ω_z+r*ω_w, top measure π*(ω_z∧ω_w), and raw mass one. Self-intersection is 7/4, not that mass.

This is a strengthened failure of recovery from the specified entire ideal/nonpluripolar tower. It does not assert equality of every conceivable movable datum or give a negative answer to original P14.4. The full polar current retained in n1 already differs. No other atom is claimed solved. notes.text:
This is an application of the sole supplied mathematical grant B in its exact domain, using n1's proved surface geometry. It is not an extension to complex P-types, analytic approximation, nonprojective geometry or real transcendental classes.

For positive rational a,b,c over the algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field C, take L=π*O_Y(b,c)+aE. Restriction of a cleared-degree section to E has degree −ℓa. Repeated division by E until this degree becomes zero proves H0(X,ℓL)=σ_E^(ℓa)H0(X,π*O_Y(ℓb,ℓc)). Residual sections descend across the smooth surface point by the local Hartogs expansion. Their bundle A is generated, so the actual moving/fixed pair is A=π*O_Y(b,c), T=aE.

B's zero-weight full system gives q_T(v)=−a v(I_E) at all points, including supports, because some moving generator is a unit at every center. It is the normalized minimal reference: nearby actual bundles B_i force E-vanishing at least −ℓ B_i·E in degree ℓ. That coefficient tends to a, and incoming generic constants tend to zero. The endpoint bound u≤q_T therefore holds divisorially and at v0, then everywhere by B's all-point order determination.

For the stationary product moving model C=pr_X*A+dF, A²=2bc and C³=3d(2bc). B's finite raw energy is C³/3−dA²=0. Its sole central component has multiplicity one, valuation v0 and restriction square 2bc; the component formula gives raw measure 2bc δ_v0. This is an actual operator calculation retaining aE. The complex ν=0 state instead has measure 2bc π*(ω_z∧ω_w) on a different carrier. No equality or canonical pushforward is established. Same-shadow states ν=sμ_i have complex mass 2c(b−s); they are not compatible DXZ test curves and contradict no DXZ comparison theorem.
